    White Knight Diner (0.2 miles)<\/strong>
    <\/span>Tiny restaurant serving classic American diner food, open for breakfast and lunch. No online menu.<\/span><\/p>

    Syberg\u2019s on Market<\/a> (0.3 miles)<\/strong>
    <\/span>Local restaurant\/sports bar serving classic American fare, with a focus on seafood. Menu includes many St. Louis favorites including Toasted Ravioli, thin-crust Pizza, and the option to add Provel cheese (loved by locals, hated by nearly everyone else). Wheelchair accessible. Menus download as PDFs that aren\u2019t totally accessible, but you can access the text and costs.<\/span><\/p>

    Idol Wolf<\/a> (inside 21C Museum Hotel St. Louis) (0.4 miles)
    <\/strong>Swanky Spanish restaurant in a brand new art hotel. Go here for Tapas and cocktails.
    <\/strong><\/p>

    IMO\u2019S Pizza<\/a> (0.6 miles)\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>Local chain that serves St. Louis Style Pizza: a thin cracker-like crust topped with gooey Provel cheese. This polarizing pizza has many devoted fans, and is worth trying for the adventurous. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Levels Nigerian Cuisine<\/a> (0.6 miles)
    <\/strong>Delicious new Nigerian spot in Downtown St. Louis with an atmospheric dining room.<\/p>

    Simply Delicious<\/a> (0.6 miles)
    <\/strong>Casual breakfast and brunch spot with delicious and luxurious bites<\/p>

    The Biscuit Joint<\/a> (0.7 miles)
    <\/strong>Brand new and hotly anticipated fast casual purveyor of excellent Biscuits in midtown. Open for Breakfast and Lunch.     Online menu.<\/a><\/p>

    Havana's Cuisine Restauran<\/a>t (0.7 miles) <\/strong>\u00a0
    <\/span>Fast casual restaurant with incredible Cuban sandwiches and limited seating \u2013 open for lunch only. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Kain Tayo Filipino Cuisine<\/a> (0.7 miles)\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>Delicious filipino food in a spacious dining room. Menu is not accessible<\/span><\/p>

    Mizu Sushi Bar<\/a> (0.8 miles)
    <\/strong>Popular Sushi restaurant in a classic downtown building<\/p>

    Pharaoh\u2019s Donuts<\/a> (0.8 miles)\u00a0<\/strong>
    In a city filled with amazing donut places, this Black-owned downtown mainstay distinguishes itself as one of the best. Counter-service, no seating. No online menu.<\/span><\/p>

    Rooster<\/a> (0.9 miles)\u00a0<\/strong>
    Popular restaurant serving contemporary spins on brunch and lunch classics. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is a PDF and not accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Pappy\u2019s Smokehouse<\/a> (1.1 miles)\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>Popular local BBQ restaurant, known for their ribs. Not wheelchair accessible. Menu is a PDF and not accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    The Fountain on Locust<\/a> (1.1 miles)\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>Decadent old-fashioned soda fountain with art deco decor, and a big menu of soups, salads, sandwiches and ice cream sundaes. Its bathroom was once voted the best bathroom in the United States. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is an accessible PDF.<\/span><\/p>

    Ballpark Village<\/a> (1.1 miles)<\/strong>\u00a0
    Complex next to Busch Stadium with numerous restaurants and bars.\u00a0 Katie\u2019s Pasta & Pizza and Salt & Smoke (BBQ) are two highlights. Most locations are wheelchair accessible. Menus are difficult to locate online, and the ones you can find lead to an online ordering website rather than a list of food and prices.<\/span><\/p>

    Bulrush<\/a> (1.4 miles)\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>Award-winning restaurant serving seasonal tasting menus inspired by historic regional Ozark cuisine with locally sourced ingredients.\u00a0 A unique experience, albeit an expensive one. Reservations essential. Menu is not accessible<\/span><\/p>","_id":"202abf4"},{"tab_title":"Farther Afield","tab_content":"

    Lona\u2019s Lil Eats<\/a>\u00a0<\/strong>
    Informal and cheery restaurant featuring rice paper wraps and other dishes inspired by the Yunnan province in China, a fusion of northern Thai and southern Chinese cuisine. Not wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Balkan Treat Box<\/a>\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>St. Louis is home to the largest Bosnian population outside of Bosnia & Herzegovina. Of the many incredible Bosnian restaurants in the area, this one is one of the most celebrated.\u00a0 Open for lunch only. Wheelchair accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    J\u2019s Pitaria<\/strong><\/a> is further away, but also serves great Bosnian food and is open for dinner.\u00a0Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Lefty\u2019s Fried Rice <\/strong><\/a>
    Black-owned Chinese-American Restaurant.\u00a0 In addition to an extensive menu of fried rice, Lefty\u2019s is known for St. Paul\u2019s sandwiches, a St. Louis area staple at Chinese-American restaurants. Takeout can be delivered to the conference hotel. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is screen-reader-friendly, but you can\u2019t navigate the page with keyboard only.<\/span><\/p>

    City Foundry<\/strong><\/a> \u00a0<\/span>
    <\/span>Food hall located in a former foundry, which also includes shops, a cinema, and a music venue.\u00a0 Sure Este (Mexican\/Yucatan cuisine) is one of the most highly regarded vendors there. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.<\/span>\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

    Gioia\u2019s Deli<\/a>\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>This sandwich shop in The Hill, St. Louis\u2019s Little Italy, is famous for the Hot Salami Sandwich, rated the best sandwich in Missouri by <\/span>Food & Wine Magazine. <\/span><\/i>Wheelchair accessible. Menu is an accessible PDF.<\/span><\/p>

    La Patisserie Chouquette<\/a>\u00a0<\/strong>
    Bakery specializing in lavish French-inspired pastries. Wheelchair accessible from side entrance. Menu is not accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Sameem Afghan Restaurant<\/a>\u00a0<\/strong>
    Intimate restaurant for authentic Afghani cuisine. Not wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Bailey\u2019s Range<\/a> <\/strong>
    Sleek modern restaurant serving burgers and ice cream, with vegan and gluten-free options. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is a PDF, and not fully accessible.<\/p>

    Sultan Mediterranean Restaurant<\/a>\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>Restaurant with delicious middle eastern food run by a Kurdish family. Highlights include the Palestinian dish Musakhan and their Turkish coffee. Not wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    SweetArt (Vegan)<\/a>\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>Restaurant and bakery renowned for their inventive vegan fare. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Terror Tacos (Vegan)<\/a>\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>Casual restaurant serving vegan tacos and burritos with a heavy metal aesthetic. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    TinyChef<\/a>\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>One of the most unique and beloved chefs in St. Louis, Melanie Meyer serves Korean fusion food out of a small kitchen space in a dive bar called the Silver Ballroom, crammed with pinball machines. Dinner Fridays-Mondays. Wheelchair accessible. No online menu.<\/span><\/p>

    Broadway Oyster Bar<\/a>\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>Cajun restaurant with delicious food, live music and a spacious outdoor patio. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Blueberry Hill<\/a>\u00a0\u00a0<\/strong>
    Diner serving classic American and St. Louis fare (T-ravs!) with a kitschy, rockabilly aesthetic. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Clementine\u2019s Naughty and Nice Creamery<\/strong><\/a> \u00a0<\/span>
    Ice cream shop with many delicious and inventive flavors, including several boozy varieties and vegan options. Not wheelchair accessible. Menu is a web page, not fully accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Ted Drewes<\/a>\u00a0\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>Classic St. Louis staple for Frozen Custard.\u00a0 You can make the trek out to its flagship at the South edge of the city or pick up a cup from a vending machine located at Lambert Airport. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible as a webpage, PDF is not accessible.<\/span><\/p>","_id":"4d747ea"}],"tab_typography_typography":"custom","tab_typography_font_family":"Figtree","tab_typography_font_size":{"unit":"px","size":"24","sizes":[]},"tab_typography_font_size_tablet":{"unit":"px","size":"42","sizes":[]},"tab_typography_font_size_mobile":{"unit":"px","size":"32","sizes":[]},"tab_typography_font_weight":"500","tab_typography_text_transform":"none","tab_typography_font_style":"normal","tab_typography_line_height":{"unit":"px","size":"60","sizes":[]},"tab_typography_line_height_tablet":{"unit":"px","size":"48","sizes":[]},"tab_typography_letter_spacing":{"unit":"px","size":"-1","sizes":[]},"__globals__":{"tab_color":"globals\/colors?id=text","tab_active_color":"globals\/colors?id=primary"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"tabs"},{"id":"6d02ca0","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Where to Drink","size":"xxl","align":"center"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"heading"},{"id":"9b1f622","elType":"widget","settings":{"tabs":[{"tab_title":"Coffee","tab_content":"

    Anchor Room Coffee House<\/a> (0.3 miles) <\/strong>\u00a0<\/strong>
    <\/span>Non-profit coffee shop inside of a Methodist church, serves coffee and sandwiches\/small bites. Menu is not accessible via keyboard.<\/span><\/p>

    Good Press (inside 21C Museum Hotel St. Louis)<\/strong><\/a> (0.4 miles)<\/strong>
    Gorgeous caf\u00e9 inside of a new art hotel with great coffee and bites for breakfast and lunch.<\/p>

    Catalyst Coffee Bar <\/a><\/strong> (0.5 miles)<\/strong>
    Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    High Low <\/a> (1.4 miles)
    <\/strong>A \u201cliterary arts cafe\u201d filled with bookshelves, connected to a gallery and event space that hosts frequent readings, and coffee served by one of the best local coffee roasters. Wheelchair accessible from side entrance. No online menu.<\/span><\/p>

    Shameless Grounds <\/a>(2.8 miles)
    <\/strong>A sex-positive coffee shop that serves breakfast and lunch items and includes a lending library of titles related to human sexuality. Not wheelchair accessible. Menu is an accessible PDF.<\/span><\/p>

    Gelataria Coffee Company<\/a> (3.5 miles)\u00a0
    <\/strong>Spacious cafe on Grand Avenue serving both coffee and gelato. Not wheelchair accessible. No online menu.<\/span><\/p>

    Cafe Dolce (4.2 miles)
    <\/strong>Italian coffee shop in The Hill with excellent espresso and delicious italian pastries. Not wheelchair accessible. No online menu.<\/span><\/p>","_id":"202abf4"},{"tab_title":"Tea","tab_content":"

    The London Tea Room <\/a> (0.3 miles)
    <\/strong>Quiet, light-filled space for lunch and afternoon tea. Menu is accessible.<\/span><\/p>","_id":"4d747ea"},{"_id":"29e0752","tab_title":"Bars","tab_content":"

    Schlafly Tap Room <\/a> (0.4 miles)
    <\/strong>Local brewery housed in a historic building.\u00a0 Also serves sandwiches and other bar food. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Brick River Cider<\/a>\u00a0(0.4 miles)
    <\/strong>The first cidery in St. Louis. Taproom with many varieties of cider, bar food and sandwiches. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    The Crack Fox<\/a> (0.6 miles)\u00a0
    <\/strong>Downtown dive bar with frequent (and often LGBTQ+-centered events) including drag, karaoke. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is screen reader accessible but is low-contrast and hard to read.<\/span><\/p>

    Videira Wine Shop and Bar<\/a> (0.7 miles)
    <\/strong>Swanky new wine bar with small bites<\/p>

    Planter\u2019s House<\/a> (0.9 miles) <\/strong>St. Louis\u2019s premier cocktail bar in a chic interior with great food as well. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Urban Chestnut Midtown Biergarten and Brewery<\/a> (1.3 miles)\u00a0
    <\/strong>German-inspired brewery with a spacious outdoor patio and a limited menu of bar food. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    Sophie\u2019s Artist Lounge<\/a> (1.4 miles)\u00a0
    <\/strong>Stylish and striking cocktail lounge connected to an art gallery, with local DJs spinning many nights. Wheelchair accessible from side entrance. Menu is not accessible.<\/span><\/p>

    LGBTQ+ Bars
    <\/strong>Many are in The Grove neighborhood (2.7 miles), the central LGBTQ+ district, including self-identified gay bars Rehab, Just John, and Prism,\u00a0 and inclusive bars that attract a queer crowd like Handlebar. Other LGBTQ+ establishments of note include Bar:PM (6.6 miles) (beloved by the local leather community) and Small Change (2.5 miles) (which has a dive bar aesthetic but elevated and creative cocktails)<\/span><\/p>"}],"tab_typography_typography":"custom","tab_typography_font_family":"Figtree","tab_typography_font_size":{"unit":"px","size":"24","sizes":[]},"tab_typography_font_size_tablet":{"unit":"px","size":"42","sizes":[]},"tab_typography_font_size_mobile":{"unit":"px","size":"32","sizes":[]},"tab_typography_font_weight":"500","tab_typography_text_transform":"none","tab_typography_font_style":"normal","tab_typography_line_height":{"unit":"px","size":"60","sizes":[]},"tab_typography_line_height_tablet":{"unit":"px","size":"48","sizes":[]},"tab_typography_letter_spacing":{"unit":"px","size":"-1","sizes":[]},"__globals__":{"tab_color":"globals\/colors?id=text","tab_active_color":"globals\/colors?id=primary"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"tabs"},{"id":"e96fddc","elType":"widget","settings":{"space":{"unit":"px","size":"20","sizes":[]}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"spacer"},{"id":"96ca97b","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Where to Visit","size":"xxl","align":"center"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"heading"}],"isInner":""},{"id":"445d911","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":"16"},"elements":[],"isInner":""}],"isInner":""},{"id":"31e3c24","elType":"section","settings":{"structure":"30"},"elements":[{"id":"4a9f946","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":"33","_inline_size":"16"},"elements":[],"isInner":""},{"id":"cbe85f6","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":"33","_inline_size":"50.333"},"elements":[{"id":"3f40703","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

    Visit the gorgeous grounds of the <\/span>Gateway Arch National Park<\/span><\/a>, redesigned in 2018, the expanded museum underneath, and take a very unusual elevator to the top to see views of the city and the Mississippi River. You can also take in great views from the <\/span>St. Louis Wheel at Union Station<\/span><\/a>, located in the conference hotel complex.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

    Near the hotel is the gorgeous Beaux Arts central branch of the <\/span>St. Louis Public Library<\/span><\/a>. Explore the building and view its free exhibits.\u00a0 Other destinations for book lovers include the indie bookstores <\/span>Left Bank Books<\/span><\/a> and <\/span>Subterranean Books<\/span><\/a>, and the charming used bookstore <\/span>Hammonds Antiques & Books<\/span><\/a>.\u00a0\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

    Take a short walk from the conference hotel to view Pillars of the Valley<\/a>, a recently unveiled public art installation by local artist Damon Davis on the southwest corner of City Park Stadium that commemorates Mill Creek Valley neighborhood and its displaced residents.\u00a0 Mill Valley was once a vibrant neighborhood with predominately Black residents that was declared blighted and razed starting in 1959 in the name of \u201curban renewal\u201d, displacing over 20,000 residents.\u00a0 The neighborhood and highway to the immediate West of the conference hotel is where Mill Creek Valley once stood.\u00a0\u00a0<\/p>

    Art lovers have several museums to choose from including the <\/span>St. Louis Art Museum<\/span><\/a> in <\/span>Forest Park<\/span><\/a>, <\/span>Pulitzer Arts Foundation<\/span><\/a> and <\/span>Contemporary Art Museum<\/span><\/a> in Midtown and the <\/span>Kemper Art Museum<\/span><\/a> just west of Forest Park on the campus of Washington University in St. Louis (all are free admission!).\u00a0 <\/span>Citygarden Sculpture Park<\/span><\/a> is close to the hotel and has works by internationally renowned contemporary Sculptors.\u00a0 Further afield is the massive <\/span>Laumeier Sculpture Park<\/span><\/a>. If history is more your thing, you can\u2019t go wrong with the <\/span>Missouri History Museum<\/span><\/a>, <\/span>Griot Museum of Black History<\/span><\/a>, the <\/span>National Blues Museum<\/span><\/a>, and <\/span>Scott Joplin House<\/span><\/a>.\u00a0 <\/span>City Museum<\/span><\/a>, located in a former shoe factory, is a museum unlike any other, and is filled with massive sculptures by the late local sculptor Bob Cassily which visitors can slide, tunnel through, and slide down.\u00a0 It is very popular with both kids and adults.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

    Visitors with a car can explore the <\/span>Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site<\/span><\/a> (in Illinois, approx. 15 minute drive from the hotel). Cahokia is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and contains several man-made mounds that made up an enormous ancient city, which at its peak in 1100 was likely more populous than London at the time.\u00a0 St. Louis once contained many mounds in its city limits made by indigenous peoples, but all but one ancient mound were flattened by white settlers. The last remaining mound in St. Louis City is the <\/span>Sugarloaf mound<\/span><\/a>, which was bought by the Osage Nation in 2008, who are maintaining and preserving the site, and they are hoping to build an interpretive center for it in the future.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

    Venture beyond downtown and midtown to explore <\/span>St. Louis\u2019s unique neighborhoods<\/span><\/a> with its many striking 19th century brick buildings, including Old North St. Louis, Central West End, Lafayette Square, and Shaw. Soulard is another historic favorite, and is home to the <\/span>historic Soulard Farmer\u2019s Market<\/span><\/a>. The Hill is a very unique little Italy, with charming delis and restaurants. Stroll down Cherokee Street to visit its many antique and vintage shops along with its taquerias, cafes, and bars. The Delmar Loop has a vintage and rockabilly charm, with several thrift shops, restaurants, and live music venues, along with the <\/span>St. Louis Walk of Fame<\/span><\/a>.<\/span><\/p>

    Get lost in <\/span>Forest Park<\/span><\/a>.\u00a0 The park is home to the <\/span>St. Louis Zoo<\/span><\/a>, <\/span>St. Louis Art Museum<\/span><\/a>, and the <\/span>Missouri History Museum<\/span><\/a>, all world-class institutions that charge no admission fee. Other highlights include the <\/span>St. Louis Science Center<\/span><\/a> (with a striking, space-age Planetarium designed by Gyo Obata) and the gorgeous Jewel Box.\u00a0 Stay outside and explore the many walking\/cycling paths, or go ice skating at <\/span>Steinberg Skating Rink<\/span><\/a>. <\/span>Tower Grove Park<\/span><\/a> is another gem, built in a Victorian style with flamboyant pavilions. Nearby are the <\/span>Missouri Botanical Gardens<\/span><\/a> (MoBot), the second-largest botanical gardens in North America.\u00a0 Get warm in the Climatron in the Botanical Gardens, which maintains a tropical temperature year-round. <\/span>Bellefontaine Cemetery<\/span><\/a> is a lovely location for a meditative walk and an exploration through St. Louis history.<\/span><\/p>

    St. Louis has a rich performing arts scene. <\/span>The Fabulous Fox<\/span><\/a> is a former movie palace converted into a venue for live events and touring broadway shows and is built in a lavish, eclectic style that is an experience in itself! <\/span>Tina: The Tina Turner Musical<\/span><\/i> will be playing during the conference, and tours of the building are offered on Saturdays. The world-renowned <\/span>St. Louis Symphony Orchestra<\/span><\/a> is the second-oldest in North America.\u00a0 They will be performing at Touhill Performing Arts Center this upcoming season and from <\/span>November 17-19 will present a program of Korngold and Dvorak<\/span><\/a>, with guest violinist Randall Goosby. The <\/span>Black Rep <\/span><\/a>\u00a0is an award-winning theater in St. Louis devoted to performing works by primarily African-American playwrights (upcoming season not yet announced).<\/span><\/p>

    St. Louis also abounds in great live music venues. <\/span>This is a pretty good list<\/span><\/a>, and visitors can check out <\/span>the Riverfront Times<\/span><\/a> for current concerts.<\/span><\/p>

    Go bowling at <\/span>Saratoga Lanes<\/span><\/a>, the oldest bowling alley of its kind west of the Mississippi, and part of the National Registry of Historic Places\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

    Enterprise Center<\/span><\/a> is home of the St. Louis Blues, the locally beloved NHL team.\u00a0 Season not yet announced.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

    The <\/span>St. Louis International Film Festival<\/span><\/a> will be held November 9-19 with many of the films being shown at the historic <\/span>Hi-Pointe Theater<\/span><\/a>. <\/span>Chase Park Plaza Cinema<\/span><\/a>, located in a hotel in the Central West End, is another favorite St. Louis destination for movie lovers.\u00a0 For more quirky programming, visit the <\/span>Arkadin Cinema<\/span><\/a>, which started as an outdoor theater during the pandemic and has since opened a chic and intimate indoor theater with a bar.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"}],"isInner":""},{"id":"db2b783","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":"25","_inline_size":"24","_inline_size_tablet":"60","margin_tablet":{"unit":"%","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"0","left":"15","isLinked":""},"margin_mobile":{"unit":"%","top":"0","right":"0","bottom":"-10","left":"0","isLinked":""},"padding":{"unit":"px","top":"0","right":"25","bottom":"0","left":"0","isLinked":""}},"elements":[{"id":"78cfa96","elType":"widget","settings":{"image":{"id":"1642","url":"https:\/\/forum2023.diglib.org\/wp-content\/uploads\/sites\/45\/2023\/06\/kirk-thornton-evaaamWSWIk-unsplash-1-scaled.jpg","alt":"Photo Local Guide:
St. Louis

[elementor-element k="d043fdf60045e8a9c231715d4380aadc" data=""]

Table of Contents

Prepare for your visit to
St. Louis, Missouri

State and Local News

  • NPR St. Louis (STLPR)
  • CLIR / DLF
  • St. Louis Post Dispatch
  • St. Louis American
  • Riverfront Times (alternative weekly, good place to look for events)
  • St. Louis Magazine (good for events, restaurants)

Venue

[elementor-element k="d043fdf60045e8a9c231715d4380aadc" data=""]

Travel/Transportation

  • Travel Accessible St. Louis (information about accessibility of transit options)
  • St. Louis Lambert International Airport
  • Transportation Options from STL Airport (red line on MetroLink goes to Union Station)
  • Metro (bus and light rail)

St. Louis-based resources

[elementor-element k="d043fdf60045e8a9c231715d4380aadc" data=""]

Context

[elementor-element k="d043fdf60045e8a9c231715d4380aadc" data=""]
  • The Broken Heart of America: St. Louis and the Violent History of the United States by Walter Johnson (Basic Books, 2020)
  • The Last Children of Mill Creek by Vivian Gibson (Belt Books, 2020)
  • Dollhouses of St. Louis (Great episode of 99% Invisible on St. Louis)
  • St. Louis LGBT History Project
  • Mapping LGBTQ St. Louis A digital humanities project exploring how LGBTQ+ St. Louis has evolved over time.

Local Guide Map

[elementor-element k="d043fdf60045e8a9c231715d4380aadc" data=""]

Where to Eat

Close By
Farther Afield
Close By

White Knight Diner (0.2 miles)
Tiny restaurant serving classic American diner food, open for breakfast and lunch. No online menu.

Syberg’s on Market (0.3 miles)
Local restaurant/sports bar serving classic American fare, with a focus on seafood. Menu includes many St. Louis favorites including Toasted Ravioli, thin-crust Pizza, and the option to add Provel cheese (loved by locals, hated by nearly everyone else). Wheelchair accessible. Menus download as PDFs that aren’t totally accessible, but you can access the text and costs.

Idol Wolf (inside 21C Museum Hotel St. Louis) (0.4 miles)
Swanky Spanish restaurant in a brand new art hotel. Go here for Tapas and cocktails.

IMO’S Pizza (0.6 miles) 
Local chain that serves St. Louis Style Pizza: a thin cracker-like crust topped with gooey Provel cheese. This polarizing pizza has many devoted fans, and is worth trying for the adventurous. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.

Levels Nigerian Cuisine (0.6 miles)
Delicious new Nigerian spot in Downtown St. Louis with an atmospheric dining room.

Simply Delicious (0.6 miles)
Casual breakfast and brunch spot with delicious and luxurious bites

The Biscuit Joint (0.7 miles)
Brand new and hotly anticipated fast casual purveyor of excellent Biscuits in midtown. Open for Breakfast and Lunch. Online menu.

Havana’s Cuisine Restaurant (0.7 miles)  
Fast casual restaurant with incredible Cuban sandwiches and limited seating – open for lunch only. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.

Kain Tayo Filipino Cuisine (0.7 miles) 
Delicious filipino food in a spacious dining room. Menu is not accessible

Mizu Sushi Bar (0.8 miles)
Popular Sushi restaurant in a classic downtown building

Pharaoh’s Donuts (0.8 miles) 
In a city filled with amazing donut places, this Black-owned downtown mainstay distinguishes itself as one of the best. Counter-service, no seating. No online menu.

Rooster (0.9 miles) 
Popular restaurant serving contemporary spins on brunch and lunch classics. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is a PDF and not accessible.

Pappy’s Smokehouse (1.1 miles) 
Popular local BBQ restaurant, known for their ribs. Not wheelchair accessible. Menu is a PDF and not accessible.

The Fountain on Locust (1.1 miles) 
Decadent old-fashioned soda fountain with art deco decor, and a big menu of soups, salads, sandwiches and ice cream sundaes. Its bathroom was once voted the best bathroom in the United States. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is an accessible PDF.

Ballpark Village (1.1 miles) 
Complex next to Busch Stadium with numerous restaurants and bars.  Katie’s Pasta & Pizza and Salt & Smoke (BBQ) are two highlights. Most locations are wheelchair accessible. Menus are difficult to locate online, and the ones you can find lead to an online ordering website rather than a list of food and prices.

Bulrush (1.4 miles) 
Award-winning restaurant serving seasonal tasting menus inspired by historic regional Ozark cuisine with locally sourced ingredients.  A unique experience, albeit an expensive one. Reservations essential. Menu is not accessible

Farther Afield

Lona’s Lil Eats 
Informal and cheery restaurant featuring rice paper wraps and other dishes inspired by the Yunnan province in China, a fusion of northern Thai and southern Chinese cuisine. Not wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.

Balkan Treat Box 
St. Louis is home to the largest Bosnian population outside of Bosnia & Herzegovina. Of the many incredible Bosnian restaurants in the area, this one is one of the most celebrated.  Open for lunch only. Wheelchair accessible.

J’s Pitaria is further away, but also serves great Bosnian food and is open for dinner. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.

Lefty’s Fried Rice
Black-owned Chinese-American Restaurant.  In addition to an extensive menu of fried rice, Lefty’s is known for St. Paul’s sandwiches, a St. Louis area staple at Chinese-American restaurants. Takeout can be delivered to the conference hotel. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is screen-reader-friendly, but you can’t navigate the page with keyboard only.

City Foundry  
Food hall located in a former foundry, which also includes shops, a cinema, and a music venue.  Sure Este (Mexican/Yucatan cuisine) is one of the most highly regarded vendors there. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible. 

Gioia’s Deli 
This sandwich shop in The Hill, St. Louis’s Little Italy, is famous for the Hot Salami Sandwich, rated the best sandwich in Missouri by Food & Wine Magazine. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is an accessible PDF.

La Patisserie Chouquette 
Bakery specializing in lavish French-inspired pastries. Wheelchair accessible from side entrance. Menu is not accessible.

Sameem Afghan Restaurant 
Intimate restaurant for authentic Afghani cuisine. Not wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.

Bailey’s Range
Sleek modern restaurant serving burgers and ice cream, with vegan and gluten-free options. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is a PDF, and not fully accessible.

Sultan Mediterranean Restaurant 
Restaurant with delicious middle eastern food run by a Kurdish family. Highlights include the Palestinian dish Musakhan and their Turkish coffee. Not wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.

SweetArt (Vegan) 
Restaurant and bakery renowned for their inventive vegan fare. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.

Terror Tacos (Vegan) 
Casual restaurant serving vegan tacos and burritos with a heavy metal aesthetic. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.

TinyChef 
One of the most unique and beloved chefs in St. Louis, Melanie Meyer serves Korean fusion food out of a small kitchen space in a dive bar called the Silver Ballroom, crammed with pinball machines. Dinner Fridays-Mondays. Wheelchair accessible. No online menu.

Broadway Oyster Bar 
Cajun restaurant with delicious food, live music and a spacious outdoor patio. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.

Blueberry Hill  
Diner serving classic American and St. Louis fare (T-ravs!) with a kitschy, rockabilly aesthetic. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.

Clementine’s Naughty and Nice Creamery  
Ice cream shop with many delicious and inventive flavors, including several boozy varieties and vegan options. Not wheelchair accessible. Menu is a web page, not fully accessible.

Ted Drewes  
Classic St. Louis staple for Frozen Custard.  You can make the trek out to its flagship at the South edge of the city or pick up a cup from a vending machine located at Lambert Airport. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible as a webpage, PDF is not accessible.

Where to Drink

Coffee
Tea
Bars
Coffee

Anchor Room Coffee House (0.3 miles)  
Non-profit coffee shop inside of a Methodist church, serves coffee and sandwiches/small bites. Menu is not accessible via keyboard.

Good Press (inside 21C Museum Hotel St. Louis) (0.4 miles)
Gorgeous café inside of a new art hotel with great coffee and bites for breakfast and lunch.

Catalyst Coffee Bar (0.5 miles)
Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.

High Low (1.4 miles)
A “literary arts cafe” filled with bookshelves, connected to a gallery and event space that hosts frequent readings, and coffee served by one of the best local coffee roasters. Wheelchair accessible from side entrance. No online menu.

Shameless Grounds (2.8 miles)
A sex-positive coffee shop that serves breakfast and lunch items and includes a lending library of titles related to human sexuality. Not wheelchair accessible. Menu is an accessible PDF.

Gelataria Coffee Company (3.5 miles) 
Spacious cafe on Grand Avenue serving both coffee and gelato. Not wheelchair accessible. No online menu.

Cafe Dolce (4.2 miles)
Italian coffee shop in The Hill with excellent espresso and delicious italian pastries. Not wheelchair accessible. No online menu.

Tea

The London Tea Room (0.3 miles)
Quiet, light-filled space for lunch and afternoon tea. Menu is accessible.

Bars

Schlafly Tap Room (0.4 miles)
Local brewery housed in a historic building.  Also serves sandwiches and other bar food. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is not accessible.

Brick River Cider (0.4 miles)
The first cidery in St. Louis. Taproom with many varieties of cider, bar food and sandwiches. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.

The Crack Fox (0.6 miles) 
Downtown dive bar with frequent (and often LGBTQ+-centered events) including drag, karaoke. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is screen reader accessible but is low-contrast and hard to read.

Videira Wine Shop and Bar (0.7 miles)
Swanky new wine bar with small bites

Planter’s House (0.9 miles) St. Louis’s premier cocktail bar in a chic interior with great food as well. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.

Urban Chestnut Midtown Biergarten and Brewery (1.3 miles) 
German-inspired brewery with a spacious outdoor patio and a limited menu of bar food. Wheelchair accessible. Menu is accessible.

Sophie’s Artist Lounge (1.4 miles) 
Stylish and striking cocktail lounge connected to an art gallery, with local DJs spinning many nights. Wheelchair accessible from side entrance. Menu is not accessible.

LGBTQ+ Bars
Many are in The Grove neighborhood (2.7 miles), the central LGBTQ+ district, including self-identified gay bars Rehab, Just John, and Prism,  and inclusive bars that attract a queer crowd like Handlebar. Other LGBTQ+ establishments of note include Bar:PM (6.6 miles) (beloved by the local leather community) and Small Change (2.5 miles) (which has a dive bar aesthetic but elevated and creative cocktails)

Where to Visit

[elementor-element k="d043fdf60045e8a9c231715d4380aadc" data=""]

What to Do

[elementor-element k="d043fdf60045e8a9c231715d4380aadc" data=""]

CLIR Events Sponsorship

The 2023 Digital Library Federation (DLF) Forum and affiliated events are multi-day experiences for learning, networking, and skill-building, working to inspire, connect, and share successes and failures with a dedicated community of digital library practitioners. We are eager to host a safe, inclusive, in-person event in St. Louis, MO, based on the guiding principle of intentionality. We’re excited to share sponsorship opportunities for our in-person events soon. Want to learn more about sponsorship sooner? Let us know through this form.

item.title: Sponsors
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
Sponsors

Thank you to our 2023 CLIR Events sponsors!

★ 2023 CLIR Events exhibitor

Exhibitors will be present at the events. Stop by their tables to say hello if you're joining us in St. Louis!

Platinum

Platinum Sponsor

AVP ★

AVP (weareavp.com) offers consulting services to help make your digital assets and media easier to find, share, protect, and put to good use. From Insights to implementation, AVP delivers results: We believe that consultation should go beyond delivering reports. Our actionable deliverables have real-world impact, guiding you from insights to implementation and beyond. We equip you with the knowledge and tools you need to action your strategies.

  • Visit their website

Gold

Gold + Lanyards Sponsor

AM Quartex ★

AM’s digital collections and technology platforms enrich the study, research and teaching of primary sources. AM works with libraries, archives and heritage institutions to digitise the world’s historical and cultural knowledge. Developed to present AM's own primary source collections, Quartex helps customers bring archival materials to life.

  • Visit their website
Gold + Swag Sponsor

TIND ★

TIND has developed the TIND Digital Archive, a tool to showcase and preserve any digital collection, including photographs, books, manuscripts, newspapers and audiovisual material.

TIND is an official CERN spin-off providing library management systems, digital preservation- and research data management solutions based on CERN open source software.

  • Visit their website

Silver

Silver Sponsor

Lyrasis ★

Lyrasis is a community-supported non-profit whose mission is to support enduring access to our shared academic, scientific and cultural heritage for archives, libraries, museums and research communities. Lyrasis offers technologies, services and special programs designed by and for knowledge professionals and brings together more than 2000 collections-holding organizations worldwide for collaboration, innovation and scale. Lyrasis is the organizational home to ArchivesSpace, BiblioLabs, CollectionSpace, DSpace, Fedora, VIVO, ORCID US and The Palace Project.

Silver Sponsor

StackMap ★

StackMap is an indoor mapping web application for your library. We've assisted libraries all over the world by:
- Providing users with a map and written directions directly to their desired item right from your library's catalog or discovery layer.
-Allowing your users to see which computers are available at a given time while also highlighting any specialty software and hardware.
-Helping your users see where rooms and places of interest are located in a facility: study rooms, lecture halls, conference spaces, offices, restrooms, elevators and more.

Silver Sponsor

Paperboy Digital
Consulting ★

Paperboy Digital Consulting will help you take ownership of your archival digitization program to create Open Access collections in support of the Digital Humanities. Paperboy can manage the full project lifecycle. From ideation, to funding, to project and vendor management, Paperboy will be there to support you and deliver a smooth and efficient project.

We work with all archival formats — Books, ephemera, maps, periodicals, recordings, and more; including metadata capture. We help you pick the project. We help you find funding for the project. We help you manage the project. Your content gets digitized.

Silver Sponsor

4Science ★

4Science is a Certified Platinum Provider of DSpace and major contributor to DSpace 7. We’re proud to be seen as anticipators of innovation thanks to outstanding solutions for research information & data management and cultural heritage. 4Science’s true mission is to contribute actively and substantially to the global open scholarly infrastructure, enabling institutions to share their knowledge and expertise sustainably, via fully interoperable systems and standards. Our solutions include DSpace, its extensions CRIS and GLAM, Dataverse, and OJS. Our services range from installation and configuration to hosting and maintenance, from customization to integration, training, and consultancy.

Purdue University Libraries and School of Information Studies ★

At Purdue Libraries, our mission is to lead in research, teaching, and learning, and create and provide equitable access to diverse resources, outstanding services, and innovative space, for Purdue’s local, national, and international communities. item.title: Fellowships
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
DLF Forum
Fellowships

The deadline to apply has passed. Meet this year's awardees.

In the spirit of DLF’s long-standing commitment to being an open, inclusive community, welcoming members from all parts of the digital library, museum, archives, and cultural heritage sectors, and making every effort to connect conversations that extend beyond our organizational borders, through Forum Fellowships DLF welcomes new, dynamic voices and valuable perspectives that have enriched our events and larger community. 

DLF Forum Fellowships will include: 

  • A complimentary room at the conference hotel for three nights (November 12-14)
  • A stipend for travel and incidentals ($650)
  • Invitations to special networking opportunities


GLAM Cross-Pollinator and DLF Forum Fellowships will include the following:

  • Complimentary DLF Forum registration 


In return, Fellows agree to share a brief (500 word) reflection on their experiences to be published on the DLF blog after the Forum.

Read more about each opportunity below and apply by completing this application. Applicants will not receive more than one award but may apply for as many awards as they are eligible. 

We purposely keep our Fellowship applications lightweight, so applicants only need to answer a few basic questions, provide a brief personal statement (500 word max), and share a copy of your resume/C.V. or a link to your online professional profile. If you have any questions about this year’s opportunities or application process, contact Team DLF at awards@diglib.org.

Award Categories

The following awards are being offered in 2023:

DLF Forum Fellowships (2)

About the Opportunity

The DLF community includes many who work in libraries and other information and cultural institutions who are lively, intellectually engaged, and inquisitive, but who are not always routinely funded to travel to conferences where they can learn more about the field, see digital initiatives from other institutions, and meet leaders in the profession. 

Eligibility

  • This award is open to digital library, archives, museum, and arts & cultural heritage students and professionals. We especially encourage applications from individuals who identify as Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC), individuals working at Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs), Tribal Colleges and Universities (TCUs), and other libraries, archives, museums, and organizations that center BIPOC to promote inclusivity to the greatest extent possible.
    • Self-identification options will be provided in the application form but are not required.
  • All are welcome to apply, including those who do not work or study at a DLF member organization, but preference will be given to applicants who have never received a prior Forum Fellowship award.
GLAM Cross-Pollinator Registration Awards

About the Opportunity

Museum and library staff face similar challenges in the digital landscape and yet have too few opportunities to come together. Through partnerships with other GLAM (Galleries, Libraries, Archives, and Museums) organizations, we strive to bring new voices and perspectives to our Forum and to send accomplished DLF practitioners to valuable conferences they might not otherwise visit. In 2023, DLF continues its tradition of “cross-pollination” with DLF community partners, offering complimentary registration to a representative from each of our partner organizations: ARLIS/NA (Art Libraries Society of North America), ASIS&T (Association for Information Science and Technology) and ER&L (Electronic Resources and Libraries).

Please note that GLAM Cross-Pollinator Registration Awards provide only DLF Forum Registration. Other costs must be covered by the attendee/their employer.

Thanks to our partners at ARLIS/NA, ASIS&T, and ER&L for making reciprocal registration awards available to DLF members in 2023!

Eligibility Requirements

To be eligible for these registration awards, an applicant must be a member in good standing of one of the three organizations listed above.

The deadline to apply has passed.

The DLF Forum Fellowship Committee, made up of community volunteers, made award decisions and applicants were notified of their status in mid-July.

Support inclusivity at the Forum by helping us bring new and engaged professionals to the event. Find out how your organization can sponsor our Forum Fellowships today.

Learn More

DLF Forum Fellowships (2)

About the Opportunity

The DLF community includes many who work in libraries and other information and cultural institutions who are lively, intellectually engaged, and inquisitive, but who are not always routinely funded to travel to conferences where they can learn more about the field, see digital initiatives from other institutions, and meet leaders in the profession. 

Eligibility

  • This award is open to digital library, archives, museum, and arts & cultural heritage students and professionals. We especially encourage applications from individuals who identify as Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC), individuals working at Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs), Tribal Colleges and Universities (TCUs), and other libraries, archives, museums, and organizations that center BIPOC to promote inclusivity to the greatest extent possible.
    • Self-identification options will be provided in the application form but are not required.
  • All are welcome to apply, including those who do not work or study at a DLF member organization, but preference will be given to applicants who have never received a prior Forum Fellowship award.
GLAM Cross-Pollinator Registration Awards

About the Opportunity

Museum and library staff face similar challenges in the digital landscape and yet have too few opportunities to come together. Through partnerships with other GLAM (Galleries, Libraries, Archives, and Museums) organizations, we strive to bring new voices and perspectives to our Forum and to send accomplished DLF practitioners to valuable conferences they might not otherwise visit. In 2023, DLF continues its tradition of “cross-pollination” with DLF community partners, offering complimentary registration to a representative from each of our partner organizations: ARLIS/NA (Art Libraries Society of North America), ASIS&T (Association for Information Science and Technology) and ER&L (Electronic Resources and Libraries).

Please note that GLAM Cross-Pollinator Registration Awards provide only DLF Forum Registration. Other costs must be covered by the attendee/their employer.

Thanks to our partners at ARLIS/NA, ASIS&T, and ER&L for making reciprocal registration awards available to DLF members in 2023!

Eligibility Requirements

To be eligible for these registration awards, an applicant must be a member in good standing of one of the three organizations listed above.

item.title: Meet the Fellows
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
Meet the
DLF Forum Fellows

With a deep-rooted dedication to fostering an inclusive and diverse community, DLF embraces members from all corners of the digital library, museum, archives, and cultural heritage sectors. Through our Forum Fellowships and GLAM Cross-Pollinator Registration Awards, we enthusiastically welcome new voices and perspectives that have greatly enriched our events and the broader community we value. In this spirit, we are thrilled to introduce you to this year's Fellows. We also invite you to read reflections written by current and past Fellows on the DLF website.

Forum Fellows

Evelyn Davis

Hello, My name is Evelyn Davis and consider myself the HBCU archivist. I am a Processing Archivist and Digital Humanities Librarian at Prairie View A&M University in Prairie View, Tx. I assist with helping the university re-discover their history since PVAMU is the second oldest university in the state of Texas. While obtaining my dual master's degrees, I had a passion and interest in African American Studies within Special Collections, so when I got the offer to work at an HBCU, I am honored to become a part of a rich history and legacy of families here in Prairie View, Tx. My other hobbies include writing poetry, dancing, bowling, painting artwork, exploring my local museums, blogging, and podcasting. Additionally, I am a Louisiana native, born in the New Orleans area and greatly influenced by my Creole heritage to embrace different cultures and having the need to preserve historical places. As a result, my love for cultural preservation started out combining my passion for writing and wanting to preserve stories at the same time. So, I am happy to continue my journey into Black Librarianship and strive to help communities preserve their stories for future generations.

Azad Namazie

Azad Namazie is a digital preservationist in training and mixed media artist pursuing their MLIS at UCLA on the Informatics and Special Collections track. They are interested in the preservation and management of mixed media collections (born-digital, oral history, AV, ephemeral) and collection data with a critical eye toward privacy, access, consent, and affect. Post-grad, they would like to do digital preservation and content management work for cultural heritage institutions. Currently, they work at the UCLA Center for Oral History Research and the Digital Library Program. They are also an incoming Andrew W. Mellon Community Archives Fellow at the Skid Row History Museum and Archive. Previously, they have worked at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA) and Los Angeles Public Library (LAPL). Other interests include: soccer, visual poetry, sci fi/fantasy novels, shoegaze, cardamom tea, esoteric escapades, and full moons.

GLAM Cross-Pollinators

Larry Eames
ARLIS/NA

Larry Eames (he/him, Mx.) is the Digital Curation and Scholarship Librarian and the liaison to English, Theatre & Dance, Art History, and Visual Art at the Kraemer Family Library at the University of Colorado Colorado Springs. He works closely with KFL’s storytelling program, using digital collections and exhibits to highlight the work of UCCS students, faculty, and the Colorado Springs community. His research deals with student citation practices and library liaison work. In his spare time, he embroiders and plays maybe a little too much D&D. You can find him as @liblarrian on Twitter, Instagram, Goodreads, and Letterboxd.

Marianne Swierenga
ASIS&T

Marianne Swierenga is the Cataloging and Metadata Librarian at Western Michigan University where she provides oversight to metadata creation and cataloging for library collections. She has a MLIS is from Wayne State University and a MFA in creative writing from Western Michigan University. As a member of the Metadata Committee of the Michigan Service Hub of the Digital Public Library of America she assists in funneling digital collections from the Western Michigan sub-hub into DPLA. And as chair of the steering committee for the Linked Data Users Group of the Midwest Collaborative for Library Services, she has been able to host a couple really exciting Wikidata edit-a-thons. Her research interests include the future of library systems, metadata creation and management, and linked data in libraries.

item.title: Calls for Proposals for DLF Forum and Learn@DLF
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
Calls for Proposals for DLF Forum and Learn@DLF

The Calls for Proposals for the DLF Forum and Learn@DLF closed on May 1.
Thank you for your interest in our events.
We hope to see you in St. Louis!

CLIR’s Digital Library Federation (DLF) invites proposals for the 2023 DLF Forum (November 13-15) and our pre-conference workshop day, Learn@DLF (November 12), which will be held in-person at the St. Louis Union Station Hotel in St. Louis, Missouri. 

A separate call has been issued for Digital Preservation 2023, the annual conference of the NDSA (November 15-16), to be held in conjunction with the Forum this year.

The submission deadline for all events is Monday, May 1, 2023, at 11:59pm ET


About Us and Our Events

The Digital Library Federation’s mission is advancing research, learning, social justice, and the public good through the creative design and wise application of digital library technologies. The DLF Forum, our signature event, is a conference explicitly designed to enact and support the community's values. Learn@DLF is our pre-conference workshop day designed to help folks take a deep dive into skills and topics that interest them. We strive to create a safe, accessible, welcoming, and inclusive atmosphere in all of our events that reflects our Code of Conduct. 

Who Attends

The DLF Forum and Learn@DLF attendees are a multi-disciplinary cross-sector audience of people who work in the digital library, museum, archives, and cultural heritage fields, from librarians, project managers, curators, technologists, and developers to administrators and service providers. The Forum welcomes practitioners from academic, art and cultural heritage, and non-profit organizations, government agencies, and more. They come from all over the country and world and represent all levels of professional experience. Forum attendees are inquisitive, engaged, and action-oriented with a focus on learning new skills and solving problems together.

We Encourage Proposals From

  • DLF members and non-members;
  • Regulars and newcomers;
  • Digital library practitioners from all sectors (higher education, museums and cultural heritage, public libraries, archives, etc.) and those in adjacent fields such as institutional research and educational technology;
  • Students, early- and mid-career professionals, and senior staff alike.


Submissions and Evaluation

Please note: Due to pre-pandemic contracts, all sessions for the 2023 DLF Forum and Learn@DLF will take place in person. We look forward to exploring potential alternate event formats in the future.

Based on community feedback and the work of our Program Committee, we welcome submissions geared toward a practitioner audience that:

  • Clearly engage with DLF’s mission;
  • Activate and inspire participants to think, make, and do;
  • Engage people from different backgrounds, experience levels, and disciplines; and/or
  • Include clear takeaways that participants can integrate and implement in their own work.


We especially welcome proposals from individuals who bring diverse professional and life experiences to the conference, including those from underrepresented or historically excluded racial, ethnic, or religious backgrounds, immigrants, veterans, those with disabilities, and people of all sexual orientations or gender identities. As we have done in the past, the Program Committee will prioritize submissions from individuals who identify as Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC), individuals working at Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs), Tribal Colleges and Universities (TCUs), and other libraries, archives, museums, and organizations that center BIPOC to promote inclusivity to the greatest extent possible. Self-identification options will be provided in the proposal submission form but are not required.  

All submissions will be peer reviewed. Reviewers will use this rubric to rate each proposal based on the values listed above. They may also recommend the proposal for a shorter format.

Broader DLF community input will also be solicited through an open community voting process, which will inform the Program Committee’s final decisions. 

We strongly encourage prospective presenters to review our Resources for Forum Presenters and Facilitators page, Rubric, and past DLF Forum programs (from 2022, 2021, and 2020) to understand what makes a successful DLF Forum proposal. Strong proposals will demonstrate how presenters intend to design their proposed sessions to be interactive, inclusive, and action-oriented and will also outline clear learning objectives.

Additional information to foster well-balanced sessions and represent as many voices as possible:

  • While there is no limit to the number of authors listed on a proposal, each submission type lists a maximum number of presenters. 
  • Further, individuals may present only once at the 2023 DLF Forum.
    • This policy applies whether one is the submitting presenter or a secondary speaker. 
    • There is no limit to the number of non-presenting collaborators or co-authors. 
    • The speaking limit restriction does not apply to co-organizing Working Group meetings, Lightning Talks, or Learn@DLF sessions. 
  • You may submit proposals to more than one event as long as they are different.
  • Looking for co-presenters on a particular topic? Try using our 2023 CLIR Events Unofficial Program Sessions and Connections for connecting with other prospective presenters. Note that the Program Committee and CLIR+DLF Staff do not monitor the document and it is not part of the official submission process.  


Submission Formats

Sessions are invited in the following lengths and formats:

Learn@DLF, November 12:

  • 3-hour Workshops: In-depth, hands-on training sessions on specific tools, techniques, workflows, or concepts. Five facilitators maximum per submission. Q&A and discussion should be incorporated throughout in an interactive and inclusive format. Workshop organizers are asked to provide details on technology needed, participant proficiency level, and learning outcomes. Interested in presenting something longer? Consider submitting a ‘part I’ (morning session) and ‘part II’ (afternoon session) as two separate proposals. 


DLF Forum, November 13-15:

    • 45-minute Workshops: Hands-on training sessions on a specific tool, technique, workflow, or concept. Up to five facilitators are allowed per submission. Workshop organizers are asked to provide details on technology needed, participant proficiency level, and learning outcomes. Additionally, please explain in your proposal how workshops will be interactive.
    • 45-minute Working Sessions: Working sessions are open sessions for community organizers, creative problem solvers, and existing or prospective DLF working groups to begin or get feedback on in-progress projects, collaborate on addressing challenges, and discuss thought-provoking questions. Up to five facilitators are allowed per submission.
    • 35-minute Panels: A panel discussion of three to four presenters (max) on a unified topic, with an emphasis on community discussion. Proposals with representative and inclusive speaker involvement will be favored by the committee. Panels will be slotted into 45-minute sessions, leaving a minimum of 10 minutes for Q&A and discussion at the end of each session. 
    • 10-minute Presentations: A presentation by a maximum of two presenters on a single topic or project. Three Presentations will be grouped by the Program Committee based on overarching themes or ideas and will be slotted into 45-minute sessions, leaving a minimum of 10-15 minutes for Q&A and discussion at the end of each session.
    • 5-minute Lightning Talks: High-energy talks held in succession for all conference attendees. A maximum of two presenters are allowed per submission. There is no formal Q&A for lightning talks, but we encourage conversation at the reception that follows.


Proposal Requirements

  • Proposal title
  • Submission format and event
  • First and last names, organizational affiliations, and email addresses for all presenters and authors
  • Brief abstract - limited to 50 words
  • Full proposal - limited to 250 words for all formats except for panels, which are limited to 500 words
  • Five keywords for your proposal
  • Learning objectives (workshops only) - limited to 50 words; brief, clear statements about what attendees will be able to do as a result of taking your proposed workshop
  • All submissions are under a CC-BY 4.0 license, which allows for sharing and adaptation of content but which requires appropriate credit and an indication of any changes made by others. Presenters must agree to share their work under this license in the submission form.

THE SUBMISSION DEADLINE FOR ALL EVENTS IS
MONDAY, MAY 1, 2023, AT 11:59PM EASTERN TIME.

We look forward to reviewing your proposals. All who submit proposals will be notified over the summer, likely by mid-July. Accepted presenters will be offered a reduced registration rate and will be expected to register or request an extension by August 15. More information about registration can be found here.

QUESTIONS? YOU CAN REACH US AT FORUM@DIGLIB.ORG.

item.title: Registration
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
CLIR Events Registration

Registration for the DLF Forum, Learn@DLF, and NDSA’s Digital Preservation has now closed. Thank you for your interest in our events.

Registration Rates

Registration for all events closed on Friday, November 3, 2023.

The deadline to request childcare or accessibility accommodations is Monday, October 2, to provide time for CLIR to contract with local vendors.

DLF Forum, November 13-15

  • Registration includes meals: three basic continental breakfasts, two lunches, frequent coffee/snack breaks. 
  • Ticket to the conference reception (including one alcoholic or non-alcoholic beverage). 
  • DLF member organizations receive one free registration code to the DLF Forum, emailed to the main contact. Not sure who receives your organization’s code? Email us at forum@diglib.org.  


Registration Costs by Ticket Type

DLF Member Organization Representative: $0

  • One coupon code per member organization
  • View the list of current DLF Member organizations on our website


Forum Presenter: $475

  • Members or non-members
  • Notifications go out by mid-July, and a spot will be held for you
  • Presenters must register or request an extension by August 15th


DLF Member Organization Worker:
Folks who currently work at DLF Member organizations. 

  • Early bird (until August 15th): $500
  • Regular (August 16th-November 3): $550

 
Non-Member:

  • Early bird (until August 15th): $775
  • Regular (August 16th-November 3): $825


HBCU Library Alliance Members: 

  • Current workers at HBCU Library Alliance member organizations receive a 20% discount on the non-member organization rate (for the DLF Forum only).
  • Please email forum@diglib.org before registering to obtain the discount code.


LIMITED Reduced “Out-of-Pocket” Rate: $300

  • To help ease costs for attendees who are not funded by an organization and are paying completely out-of-pocket, we are offering a limited number of reduced-rate tickets
  • Please register at this rate only if you receive no outside/organizational support – on the honor system

Learn@DLF, November 12

Learn@DLF (#LearnAtDLF) is DLF’s pre-conference event structured entirely as a workshop day and full of engaging, hands-on sessions. Registration includes continental breakfast, lunch buffet, and coffee breaks.

Registration Costs by Ticket Type

  • Learn@DLF Presenter: $125
  • Regular registration: $150

NDSA’s Digital Preservation, November 15-16

NDSA’s DigiPres (#DigiPres23) is the annual conference for the NDSA. Featuring an updated schedule in 2023, DigiPres now begins Wednesday afternoon with workshops, an opening plenary, and a welcome reception. The conference ends at mid-afternoon on Thursday. Registration includes one continental breakfast, one lunch buffet, one coffee break, and a reception on Wednesday evening.

Registration Costs by Ticket Type:

  • Regular registration: $225
  • When combined with a Forum registration: $200
  • LIMITED “Out of Pocket” Tickets: $200
    • To help ease costs for attendees who are not funded by an organization and are paying completely out-of-pocket, we are offering a limited number of reduced-rate tickets. Please register at this rate only if you receive no outside/organizational support – on the honor system 

Registration for all events closes on Friday, November 3, 2023.

Registration Cancellation Policy
Refunds for registration are available until Tuesday, October 31, 2023. Refunds requested after this date will be considered on a case-by-case basis. A $30 processing fee for cancellation will be charged for all refunds. All cancellations and requests for refunds must be made in writing. Please email your request to forum@diglib.org. If you need to cancel your hotel reservation, please contact the hotel directly. 


Registration Cancellation Due to Illness
Registration cancellation due to illness 48 hours prior to the event will be fully refunded, however, documentation may be requested in order to receive a refund. If you need to cancel your hotel reservation, please contact the hotel directly. 

Need Help with Registration? 
We’d be happy to help! Please email us at forum@diglib.org.

item.title: DLF Forum and Learn@DLF Conference Session Evaluation Rubric 2023
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
DLF Forum and Learn@DLF
Conference Session Evaluation Rubric 2023

Adapted from the National Recreation and Park Association Conference Session Evaluation Rubric

Originality - 20%

The Planning Committee strives to continually present unique and exciting programs that reflect our dynamic community in an accessible way that engages participants and facilitates learning.

  • 5: Excellent - The session proposal contains highly original approaches to or new perspectives toward programming and/or topics that reflect the DLF community. Session format is informative and includes multiple ways for participants to engage. 
  • 4: Good - The session proposal contains some original approach and perspectives reflecting the DLF community while addressing content that has been covered in other ways in the past. The session has multiple elements of engagement. 
  • 3: Competent - The session proposal addresses content that is expected and needed at the DLF Forum / Learn@DLF in a manner that is fitting and expected for that content within DLF standards and has at least one element of engagement. 
  • 2: Needs Improvement - The session proposal may be appropriate for the DLF Forum / Learn@DLF, but with some alteration to provide a unique and original stance with no elements of engagement. (i.e., The same session was delivered elsewhere but may be good if a different approach is taken) 
  • 1: Not Original - The session proposal demonstrates content that has been covered at length, has been presented on before by the listed speakers, or does not meet the suggested standards of a DLF Forum / Learn@DLF session. 

Relevance - 20%

DLF seeks sessions that are of great interest to prospective attendees and clearly benefit the professional needs of the DLF community. The topic is important to the field and the communities we serve and is timely. 

  • 5: Excellent - This session proposal represents forward-looking content that reflects emerging trends and current needs of the profession, the communities we serve, and is timely. 
  • 4: Good - The session proposal demonstrates content that is timely and relevant to the profession and the communities we serve and includes either an emerging trend OR current need. 
  • 3: Competent - The session proposal demonstrates content that is relevant to the audience but may perpetuate a topic area that has plenty of coverage. 
  • 2: Needs Improvement - The session topic may meet the audience, theme, and context of the DLF Forum / Learn@DLF with some adjustment.
  • 1: Not Relevant - The session proposal is not relevant to the DLF Forum / Learn@DLF audience. 

Diversity & Inclusion - 20%

The sharing of different perspectives and experiences, and ways to address and include them, are essential in creating equitable programs and developing policies and organizational practices. Sessions should address or be inclusive of multiple perspectives and how difference in needs can and should be addressed. 

  • 5: Excellent - The proposal contains multiple diverse perspectives and experiences, and includes highly original approaches to address the difference of needs within the profession and provides examples of practical application. 
  • 4: Good - The session proposal demonstrates a few diverse perspectives and experiences, and includes somewhat original approaches to address the difference of needs within the profession. 
  • 3: Competent - The proposal contains at least one diverse perspective or experience, and includes approaches to address the difference of needs within the profession. 
  • 2: Needs Improvement - The proposal is a weak demonstration of different perspectives or approaches based on diverse experiences.
  • 1: Does Not Meet Standard - The proposal does not include different perspectives or approaches based on diverse experiences.

Overall Quality - 20%

DLF is dedicated to ensuring that the programs at the DLF Forum and Learn@DLF meet the highest standards of excellence with sessions that are comprehensive where topic, intent, and learning outcomes are focused, well-presented, and thoughtfully articulated. 

  • 5: Excellent - Strongly recommend this session. The quality of the proposal exceeds the highest standards of excellence for content delivery within the context of the DLF Forum / Learn@DLF. 
  • 4: Good - This proposal delivers a standard format and quality that has become expected of DLF Forum / Learn@DLF sessions. 
  • 3: Competent - The proposal is competent but may require some minor changes to be considered for the DLF Forum / Learn@DLF (i.e., Shorten title, session length, adjust methodology/learning outcomes). 
  • 2: Needs Improvement - This proposal requires adjustments if it is to be considered for the DLF Forum / Learn@DLF (i.e., Change or adjustment in speakers, topic approach, methodology). 
  • 1: Does Not Meet Standard - This proposal does not meet minimum standards for delivery at the DLF Forum / Learn@DLF. 

Reviewer’s Recommendation - 20%

The reviewer’s recommendation for the inclusion of the proposal in the conference program.

  • 5: Definitely accept - very high quality
  • 4: Probably accept - good quality
  • 3: Neutral - borderline
  • 2: Probably reject - poor quality
  • 1: Definitely reject - of little merit or inappropriate for this conference

 

Back to the CFP
